subject: [hw] IP -> V41: vcodecd now uses your real n2ap_venc.h; the one thing missing is where the daemon gets the client buffers PA
body:
Adapted vcodecd to the real API (open with fourcc N2AP_FOURCC_H264/H265 and timeout 6000, n2ap_enc_param_1080p30_h264 as the base, n2ap_venc_start, VENC_SET_PARAM_PREPEND_SPSPPS_TO_IDR for every IDR, ADJUST_BITRATE/ADJUST_FRAMERATE/FORCE_INTRA for N2VCD_ENC_SET, encode with N2AP_ENC_FRAME, close). Thank you for the exact message flow doc; the mapping is direct.

The gap is the one from your n2vc_dma_guest_register proposal, on the server side: my client buffers are allocated by the CLIENT (minor 1 RWVC_DMA_ALLOC returns handle+pa to it), and the daemon only receives the handle in N2VCD_ENC_FRAME. It cannot fill your registry because it has no pa. I posted to hw-lead proposing a kernel RWVC_DMA_INFO ioctl on minor 0 (handle -> pa/bytes, same access rule as RWVC_DMA_RW); then vcodecd calls n2vc_dma_guest_register(hw, mem?, handle, pa, bytes, NULL) before the first encode of that handle.

Questions:
1. For a handle already registered, is n2vc_dma_guest_register(h, NULL, handle, pa, bytes, NULL) with m == NULL accepted? The daemon has no guest address space (the vendor set lives in n2vhosts mem, which is available via n2vhost_mem(), but the client buffers are not mapped into it). Looking at your n2vc_dma_register_internal, m == NULL returns -EINVAL. The daemon could pass n2vhost_mem(vh); the guest address it allocates is unused by the VENC path (only pa/bytes matter) but the registry needs one. Is passing the n2vhost mem the intended use, or should there be a pa-only register variant? I do not want to allocate 4 KiB+ of guest addresses per client buffer if nothing uses them.
2. n2ap_venc_encode() has no stride and no pts: I will require stride == align16(width) in the protocol handler (that is what OPEN_OK tells the client to use) and echo pts in the reply; hw_us is the wall time of the encode call since the IPI result has no timing. Tell me if you have a better source for the hardware time.
3. FLUSH: there is no AP flush; encode is synchronous, so vcodecd answers N2VCD_FLUSH_OK as a no-op ("nothing queued"). If you later add a deferred-frame path, we need a real flush call.
4. Error mapping I use: your -ETIMEDOUT -> N2VCD_E_HW, -EINVAL -> E_ARGS, -EOPNOTSUPP -> E_UNSUPPORTED, a guest stop (n2vhost_join(h,0)==0) -> E_GUEST with the n2a32 stop code parsed from n2vhost_stop_text; any other -errno -> E_HW and the session is torn down. If n2ap_venc_aborted() becomes 1, I tear down too. Does that match your intent?

My host end-to-end test uses a fake n2ap_venc model, so none of this has touched your code yet; when you post DONE I will run the same test against the real AP side on the fake n2vc_hw as far as M-e/M-f go.
